deadline_policy.scope: Entire evaluation process, including loading, CUDA initialization, CPU reference, output comparison and teardown where present. Only separately executed builds/JIT are excluded. All 18 post-instruction runs wrapped with timeout 10s. Exit 124 means TIMEOUT (>10 s).
deadline_policy.wall_clock_note: Recorded wrapper wall can exceed 10 s by ~0.2-0.3 s due to subprocess wait polling and termination/cleanup; GNU timeout sends termination at the 10 s limit.
deadline_policy.gpu_timeout_interpretation: MiniLinq doop-gpu loads twice and completes CPU mini reference BEFORE GPU evaluation. Its bounded processes time out before a GPU evaluation time/count is emitted. This is a whole-command timeout, not evidence its GPU kernel/fixpoint alone exceeds 10 s.

versions.srdatalog_existing_changes: uv.lock modified; untracked minimal_vulreasoner, research directories, rmm_log.txt; not changed by this measurement

machine.cpu: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 5945WX 12-Cores; 24 logical CPUs
machine.vllm_note: Expected ~43.7 GB vLLM allocation was not present at initial nvidia-smi. No unrelated process was touched. Both complete datasets fit current available VRAM; no OOM observed.
machine.contention_note: Unrelated compute processes appeared in pre-deadline runs. Per-process peaks and device-wide utilization recorded. All systems run sequentially; deadline-compliant replacement runs had no sampled competing compute PID.

timing_scopes.mini_gpu: gpu_evaluation_seconds: upload, GPU layout construction, execution, download/output decoding. Excludes both fact loads, CUDA context init, CPU mini reference and exact tuple comparison. Whole process includes all those excluded stages. GPU phase split not exposed.
timing_scopes.mini_par: compute_seconds: engine.evaluate(Facts), excludes raw fact load, Rayon pool creation, printing and process startup/exit. Whole process includes them.
timing_scopes.srd_gpu: fixedpoint_seconds: unlimited device fixedpoint plus checked synchronization; excludes JIT, CSV loading, init, prepare/H2D, counts, export and teardown. prepare_plus_fixedpoint includes H2D/database construction but still no result D2H. No tuple export in measured runs.
timing_scopes.alignment: Closest available SRD counterpart to Mini GPU evaluation is prepare + fixedpoint, but Mini additionally downloads all outputs and uses a different 135-rule query versus normalized 82-rule SRD query. Do not present these as identical-work speedups.
timing_scopes.warmups: 0 explicit warmups; 3 measured fresh processes. Earlier completed runs warmed caches before deadline-compliant reruns.
timing_scopes.ignored_binary_fields: mini_par_15_threads_reference_seconds=1.28 and derived gpu_over_mini_par_reference are hard-coded cassandra-era output, NOT xalan/batik measurements.

correctness.mini_gpu: All six completed pre-deadline runs passed exact full-tuple comparison against CPU mini for all 26 outputs. Bounded GPU runs timed out and did not complete this check.
correctness.mini_par: Counts agree with mini and GPU in all completed runs; --check not requested/run.
correctness.srd_gpu: All bounded runs completed normal native shutdown and reported matching VPT counts. No SRD-to-mini tuple export comparison was performed: matching VPT counts do not establish tuple equality.
correctness.historical_reference: 2,742,413 xalan / 37,269,128 batik are historical unguarded-query catalog references. Current guarded Object[] plus exact String[] split gives 2,741,586 / 37,237,353, matching MiniLinq and catalog upstream_reference_vpt_rows.
correctness.prepared_input_issue: Initial supplied prepared/xalan failed missing java_lang_String_array. Reprepared same catalog archives into a fresh root with current adapter; historical prepared inputs left untouched. Current program remains 82 rules, 77 relations, 37 consumed inputs.
